newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: WTO chief warns against continental trade blocs.
newsitem.headline: WTO chief warns against continental trade blocs.

text.p: World Trade Organization chief Renato Ruggiero said Tuesday the Mercosur is no obstacle to aims of global trade liberalization, but he warned against the rapid growth of continental and intercontinental blocs.

Ruggiero, making a speech in Buenos Aires, warned of grave dangers to the global economy if the world were allowed to divide up into "two, three or four big continental regional areas, each one with free trade inside but a wall outside."

The WTO director-general said his organization already knew of about 100 regional trade pacts, virtually all of them making individual efforts towards total trade liberalization by around the year 2010.

"In the next few years, regional movement will move in one direction and we have to be sure there is consistent movement in the multilateral system; otherwise we risk a split of the world economy," Ruggiero told an export conference.

Asked if the Mercosur customs bloc of Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay were counterproductive, he told Reuters "Certainly not. But where problems arise is if regionalism is much faster than multilateralism, because you get different rules of the game in the different regional systems, which is in contradiction with the objective of non-discrimination."

The WTO director-general was assured by the Argentine government's Cabinet Chief Jorge Rodriguez in his speech that the emergence of big trade blocs "is a transition towards a scheme of global free trade, where we learn to practice free trade among ourselves."

Ruggiero praised the fast growth of Mercosur, which has already signed a free trade deal with Chile and is rapidly approaching similar agreements with other South American neighbors, such as the members of the Andean Pact.

"That's good," Ruggiero said in an interview after his speech. "I don't want to slow the path of regionalism, but to make faster progress in the multilateral system. Regionalism is an extremely important tool to accelerate liberalization."
